Every unit short costs 10 expectation, service level requires demand met least 90% scenarios: Everything ordinary R. max(demand - x, 0) shortfall — kinked expression prices recourse — expectation() closes scenarios; prob() measures event demand - x <= 0 across scenarios, outer >= 0.9 service level demanded probability. Two things worth saying loud. variable declared rand_var() random variable, decision variable: solver handed value rather choosing , every mention demand refers sample. scenarios drawn service model’s seed (set_scenarios), R’s set.seed() plays role solve. answer 90% service level binding: x lands sample’s 90th percentile demand (population value qnorm(0.9, 100, 15) ≈ 119.2). Without chance constraint order quantity fall critical fractile (10 - 3) / 10 = 0.7, qnorm(0.7, 100, 15) ≈ 107.9 — constraint pushes order :
code: m <- model() x <- num_var(m, "x", 0, 200)                     # decide now demand <- rand_var(m, "demand", normal(100, 15)) # learn later set_scenarios(m, 512, seed = 42)  minimize(m, 3 * x + 10 * expectation(max(demand - x, 0))) add(m, prob(demand - x <= 0) >= 0.9) m #> quicopt model: 1 variable, 1 random (512 scenarios), 1 constraint row(s) #>   min ((3 * x) + (10 * smean(max((~demand - x), 0)))) res <- solve(m) res$solution[["x"]] #> [1] 118.7283 m2 <- model() x2 <- num_var(m2, "x", 0, 200) d2 <- rand_var(m2, "demand", normal(100, 15)) set_scenarios(m2, 512, seed = 42) minimize(m2, 3 * x2 + 10 * expectation(max(d2 - x2, 0))) solve(m2)$solution[["x"]] #> [1] 107.642
